transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-19
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (NovaHealth - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Security Lead), Janelle Ruiz (Eng Manager)
---
Summary (auto): quick recap of PII/retention requirements, define benchmarks and timeline for 4-week pilot
---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving the time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya (Customer): Hi this is Priya, here.
[00:07] Liam (Customer): Liam, here.
[00:08] Janelle (Customer): Janelle here.
[00:09] Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos here, thanks.
[00:12] Maya: Cool. We're here to scope the POC around data handling — specifically prompt storage and PII redaction, retention windows, and also load/latency benchmarks that will define success. Priya, do you want to frame the business goals?
[00:25] Priya: Yes thanks. We're building a clinical triage assistant, and a lot of the prompts will contain PHI — patient names, MRNs, free text notes. For compliance we need to ensure the POC doesn't store raw prompts beyond what's essential. Ideally we want ephemeral forwarding — i.e., transient in-memory processing and only store the minimum metadata.
[00:42] Janelle: And from eng perspective we want to measure cost/latency with our expected throughput — roughly 200 qps at peak with average prompt lengths of about 450 tokens and responses ~300 tokens. That informs batching/kv cache behavior.
[00:58] Carlos: Got it. A few clarifying q's — when you say ephemeral, are you saying zero-persist by default for the pilot, or allowed to persist to logs with redaction?
[01:10] Priya: We prefer zero-persist for prompts with PHI, but we know there may be a need to persist aggregated metrics. If a provider can guarantee automatic redaction or a configurable redaction pipeline before any disk write, that would be good.
[01:23] Liam: Also audit logs are needed for who accessed the inference outputs. We need RBAC integration and a way to show redaction occurred — e.g., redaction hash or marker not the content itself.
[01:36] Maya: Yep. On Redwood side we have a few knobs — logging levels, prompt+response retention windows, and server-side redaction hooks. For hosted customers we offer an option to disable prompt storage entirely and only store tokenized metrics. For Private/VPC we support customer-managed KMS and retention configs.
[01:52] Carlos: I'll add we have a redaction pipeline that can run regex + ML-based scrubbers. It's not perfect — sometimes false positive/negative — so we recommend a review loop. Also we can implement callback webhooks that receive redaction-metadata (not raw content) for audit trails.
[02:09] Priya: Can you explain the webhook flow? If data is redacted before storage, will the webhook receive anything PII-related?
[02:16] Carlos: Webhook would receive a JSON with meta fields: request id, redaction_status, redaction_hash, model version, and truncated token counts. It would not contain original prompt text unless you explicitly enable full logging.
[02:30] Priya: Okay that's promising. We still need to know what redaction is applied — e.g., if the model redacted a date or name. The hash is helpful but we might need flagged examples for QA.
[02:41] Maya: For the POC we can provide a signed-off process: customer sends a set of sample prompts (anonymized) and designate which fields are PII. We run the pipeline and return a redaction report that maps input fields to redaction markers. That will be part of the acceptance criteria.
[02:56] Liam: On retention timing — what are the smallest windows you support? One hour, one day, 30 days?
[03:02] Carlos: For Hosted: retention tiers are 0 (never persisted), 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days. For Dedicated and Private you can configure a custom TTL and auto-purge via policy; we can set a 24-hour auto-purge for pilot.
[03:19] Janelle: If we pick 24 hours, we need to ensure backups and s3 snapshots won't retain data beyond that.
[03:25] Maya: Good call. We'll include the backup snapshot policy in the security doc — Redwood doesn't snapshot prompt logs unless retention is >30 days, but we'll confirm and share the exact storage flow.
[03:36] Priya: Benchmarks — Carlos, you mentioned running a synthetic test. What metrics will you capture?
[03:41] Carlos: We'll capture p50, p95, p99 latencies, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and tail latency under load. We'll run with identical model weights as you'd use in pilot; for the POC we expect to use an open Llama-style model quantized to int8 unless you require FP16.
[03:58] Priya: We actually plan to test two variants: the smaller faster model for latency-sensitive paths and a larger higher-quality model for complex cases. Success criteria: p95 < 300ms for small model and p95 < 1.2s for larger model under your 200 qps baseline?
[04:14] Carlos: 200 qps with those token sizes will be tough for single-GPU; we'll likely need pooling and batching. Our math: with 450 tokens in and 300 out on average, that's ~750 tokens per request -> 150k tokens/sec at 200 qps. We'll propose a benchmarking configuration that scales GPUs accordingly.
[04:33] Janelle: Can you simulate prefix caching? We have lots of repeated system prompts, so cache hit rate is important.
[04:39] Carlos: Yes, we can run experiments with a 40% prefix reuse to show KV cache benefits. That should reduce backend load significantly.
[04:47] Priya: What about prompt storage for retraining? We might want to opt-in to storing sanitized prompts for later model refinement. How would that interact with PII rules?
[04:56] Maya: We support an opt-in "sanitized prompt store" where prompts are scrubbed by customer-provided redaction patterns before storage. That would be configured per workspace and only enabled after sign-off. For the pilot we can keep that disabled until we agree on sanitization.
[05:11] Liam: Are there guarantees about model traces or embeddings? We worry about latent PII in embeddings.
[05:17] Carlos: Good point. For embeddings we can apply vector obfuscation and denylist tokens. But embeddings are considered derived data and many customers treat them as persistent. We recommend either not storing embeddings or encrypting them with your KMS and enforcing short TTL. For pilot we can set TTL to 7 days.
[05:35] Priya: For auditability we'll need a way to prove redaction occurred — perhaps a signed artifact from Redwood or a tamper-evident log?
[05:43] Maya: We can provide signed redaction receipts: a digest of original request id + redaction markers signed by Redwood's HSM key. In Private deployments you can choose your own HSM for signing. We'll include a sample receipt format in the docs.
[05:57] Janelle: On legal side, we probably need to run this by partners legal, but timeline-wise we're hoping to start pilot in early June for four weeks. Is that feasible?
[06:06] Maya: Yes, that's feasible if we align on sample data and benchmarks this week. Carlos will run bench, I'll share security docs, and Priya will send samples.
[06:15] Carlos: Quick note on failure modes — if redaction fails and raw content would have been stored, our default hosted flow would still abide by retention TTL and we can purge, but we recommend Private deployment for full control if that's a hard req.
[06:28] Priya: Understood. We prefer Hosted for speed to start but may shift to a dedicated pool if required.
[06:34] Maya: Let's define acceptance criteria for the POC: 1) Redaction report matches customer-labeled PII on 95%+ of examples; 2) Benchmarks show p95 under the agreed thresholds for each model variant at target qps; 3) Retention TTL enforced and verified with audit receipts; 4) RBAC + audit logs visible in console.
[06:58] Liam: That works. For the redaction 95% threshold, can we have a manual review step for all false negatives?
[07:04] Maya: Yes, we'll include a QA loop — SE will produce a false negative list and we can iterate.
[07:09] Priya: Any blockers for benchmarking? Do you need service account creds?
[07:13] Carlos: We only need sample prompts and a traffic profile. If you provide a small sample dataset, we'll craft synthetic traffic to mimic it. No creds required for hosted benchmarks; for dedicated we'll need network access details.
[07:24] Janelle: We'll upload the sample to the shared drive by tomorrow.
[07:27] Maya: Great. Last housekeeping: we'll also send the POC SOW template and indicate data handling options.
[07:33] Priya: Thanks everyone. That covers it for us.
[07:36] Maya: Thanks — recap and next steps will be in the follow-up email.
[07:40] (Meeting ends)
